title: Data anchor fallback tiers and SLA mapping
body:
Purpose:
This doc defines a multi-tier fallback strategy for customers that require a regional data anchor (pin) but where absolute in-region enforcement may be temporarily infeasible (outages, capacity imbalances, or emergency migrations). The goal is to provide deterministic, auditable behavior that preserves SLA commitments while minimizing data egress risk and providing operators clear decision windows for interventions.

Context and motivation:
- We've seen two recurring operational patterns: (1) a region running out of reserved capacity and failing new requests, and (2) transient network incidents between control plane and region-local agents that prevent pin verification. Currently teams apply ad-hoc fallbacks which vary by customer and operator — this doc proposes a standard, tiered policy and an associated operator flow.

Definitions (short):
- Data anchor: the region designated in the tenant's contract for primary storage and processing (the pin).
- Fallback tier: a temporary operational mode that relaxes strict anchoring under controlled constraints (tier 1..3).
- Eviction window: time window after which tenant traffic is automatically redirected to a non-anchored fallback if the issue persists and operator hasn't intervened.

High-level policy summary:
- Tier 0 (Normal): Strict anchor enforcement. All inbound requests for pinned tenants must be routed to the pinned region; cross-region routing is rejected or queued.
- Tier 1 (Local degrade, no data egress): If pinned region compute is saturated but storage gateway is healthy, allow partial request shedding and queueing with retry-backoff. No routing outside the anchor region. Short SLA impact (SLO targets reduced, customers notified).
- Tier 2 (Anchored compute fail -> read-fallback): If pinned region compute is unavailable but read-only storage is available, allow read-only operations from a regional read replica in a nearby region (reads may be permitted outside pin, writes disallowed). Data egress logged, audit evidence collected.
- Tier 3 (Emergency cross-region fallback): As last resort if Tier 2 is unviable, route both reads and writes through a substitute region. This increases latency and egress risk; only allowed with automated telemetry thresholds AND explicit operator approval for customers with strict legal charts (otherwise escalate to legal).

SLA mapping and customer tiers:
- Free / trial customers: default tolerance limited to Tier 3 automated fallback after 2 hours of unresolved capacity outage. Lower priority on operator intervention.
- Standard customers: Tier 2 allowed after 60 minutes; Tier 3 allowed only after operator explicit approval or automated policy if account has opted into cross-region fallback.
- Enterprise / contract-anchored customers: Strict enforcement of Tier 0 unless emergency declared by SRE + customer agreement. Default is manual operator flow for any change.

Telemetry thresholds that trigger tier transitions (technical signals):
- Node pool capacity exhaustion: >95% reserved GPU utilization and queuing > 120s for 5 consecutive minutes -> signal Tier 1.
- Storage gateway healthy but compute unresponsive: control plane heartbeat missing but storage API responsive -> candidate Tier 2.
- End-to-end request failures > 5% P50/P95 spike and cross-region probes failing for >10m -> candidate Tier 3 (requires approval for enterprise).

Operator runbook (step-by-step):
1) Alert fires (capacity or heartbeat) -> Run automated triage script (see linked PR for diagnostics).
2) Confirm signal validity (check metrics, synthetic probes, and recent deploys). Note incident id in incident log.
3) If candidate Tier 1: enable local queueing with backoff policy, update tenant status page, schedule 30m re-eval.
4) If candidate Tier 2: enable read-only routing to read replica; flip telemetry to audit mode (capture all request metadata, origin region, and token hashes). Notify CS for impacted customers.
5) For Tier 3: page on-call SRE and on-call legal (if customer contract flagged). Require operator acceptance in the console and record rationale and timestamps. If acceptance missing after configured eviction window (customer-specific), follow contractual default (either automated fallback or hold).
6) Post-resolution: run reconciliation job to validate data parity and run eviction-audit to produce a customer-facing report (template in linked artifacts).

Data governance and audit evidence:
- For any action that relaxes anchoring we must capture: operator id, TTL of fallback, exact routing decisions, and per-request evidence (request id, timestamp, source region, executed region).
- Evidence retention: default 90 days for non-enterprise, 365 days for enterprise customers (configurable via contract).

Implementation notes for runtime team:
- We will implement a fallback-state machine per tenant with explicit states and controlled transitions. Each state transition must be idempotent and logged.
- Add a small in-memory cache (TTL 5s) in the control plane to avoid flapping decisions when metrics are noisy.
- Expose a per-tenant "fallback-policy" config object: allowed tiers, auto-approval windows, and evidence-retention override.

Customer communication templates (short examples):
- Notification (Tier 2 enabled): "We are temporarily operating your account in read-only mode while we remediate capacity issues in [region]. No customer data has been moved outside [region] for write operations. We'll update you in 60 minutes with progress."
- Notification (Tier 3 pending operator approval): "We recommend a temporary routing change that will allow services to continue but will route some requests outside [region]. This requires your approval as per contract clause X. Contact CS to approve or decline."

Edge cases and unresolved questions (open items):
- Legal: what exact phrasing and customer consent model is acceptable for automatic Tier 3 in certain jurisdictions (EUDRB shortlist)? (Action: Legal to propose language.)
- Metrics: define exact cardinality and sampling for per-request evidence to balance costs (Action: Observability team).
- Replica parity: how to handle writes accepted in Tier 3 when re-syncing into anchor region (Action: Storage team to propose merge strategy).

Migration playground and testing plan:
- Build a simulated tenant lab with three regions (eu-west, us-east, ap-south) and synthetic load tool that can trigger each tier deterministically.
- Run chaos tests: kill node pools, disable storage gateway, saturate network links. Verify operator flow and eviction windows.
- Acceptance criteria: automated audit shows correct evidence captures for 100% of routed requests during simulated Tier 2/3.

Quick operator checklist (TL;DR):
- Verify telemetry -> decide candidate tier -> notify CS (if >30min) -> flip state in console with notes -> monitor for 30/60/120m depending on tier -> run reconciliation and upload evidence.

Appendix: sample console log entry (free text example):
- 2024-11-21T16:42Z | operator:Priya | tenant:acme-inc | action:enable-tier-2 | reason:compute-heartbeat-missing | evidence-key:ev-20241121-042 | eviction-window:90m

Notes to self:
- Will schedule a working session with storage and legal week of 2024-12-09 to close open items.
- Need quick follow-up doc on enterprise consent workflow (separate).
